newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama beefs up security along Colombian border.
newsitem.headline: Panama beefs up security along Colombian border.

text.p: Panama beefed up security on its southern jungle border on Tuesday to stop the flood of Colombian refugees fleeing violence and intercept death squads chasing after them, authorities said.
"We have established a new police station at Port Obaldia of 150 police officers in response to the problem in the area," National Police spokesman Jose Zamora said.

Police also transferred to the small port city on Panama's border with Colombia a recently established Border Police Service of about 100 men who patrol the porous border with helicopters donated from U.S. military reserves.

Panama handed out emergency aid on Monday to more than 300 Colombian refugees who crossed through the Darien Gap to Port Obaldia after leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups clashed in Colombia's violent Uraba region.

Authorities concerned by the refugee influx sent police reinforcements to try to staunch the flow of Colombians and prevent incursions by cross-border death squads. Police are investigating the deaths of five Colombians thought to have been killed on Panamanian soil by the right-wing death squads.
In recent years, thousands of Colombian refugees have fled violence in banana-producing Uraba. Most are repatriated after receiving humanitarian aid.
